credit_metrics.text: EBITDA declined by {{ebitda.change@FY2025}} to {{ebitda@FY2025}} on revenue up {{revenue.change@FY2025}}, with operating profit down {{operating_profit.change@FY2025}} to {{operating_profit@FY2025}} after the write-offs on the third runway project.

Total debt was stable at {{total_debt@FY2025}}, so gross leverage held at {{gross_leverage@FY2025}} and the group retains net cash of {{net_cash@FY2025}}, down {{net_cash.change@FY2025}} as cash was spent on the investment programme.

Cash generation weakened: FFO fell by {{ffo.change@FY2025}} to {{ffo@FY2025}} and free cash flow by {{fcf.change@FY2025}} to {{fcf@FY2025}}, with capex intensity up {{capex_intensity.change@FY2025}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2025}}.

liquidity_funding.text: Cash and cash-like investments fell by {{cash_like.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_like@FY2025}}, still comfortably above total debt of {{total_debt@FY2025}}.

Cash liquidity to revenue declined by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}}, a buffer that remains above the airport peer median of {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_median@FY2025}}.
Funding needs are modest given gross leverage of {{gross_leverage@FY2025}}, so the investment programme is largely met from internal cash rather than new borrowing.

operating_performance.text: Passengers rose by {{passengers.change@FY2025}} to {{passengers@FY2025}}, a slower rate than the {{traffic_growth@FY2024}} growth of FY2024, with traffic growth of {{traffic_growth@FY2025}} in FY2025.

Aeronautical revenue per passenger increased by {{aero_revenue_per_passenger.change@FY2025}} to {{aero_revenue_per_passenger@FY2025}}, supported by charge adjustments under the price-cap formula and partly offset by higher temporary winter incentives.
Personnel expenses rose on collective wage increases and additions to personnel provisions, which weighed on the cost base against the revenue growth.

peer_positioning.text: Flughafen Wien has the lowest net leverage of the airport group ({{net_leverage.peer_rank@FY2025}}), at {{net_leverage@FY2025}} against a peer median of {{net_leverage.peer_median@FY2025}}, and the lowest gross leverage ({{gross_leverage.peer_rank@FY2025}}).
Cash liquidity to revenue is the strongest of the group ({{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_rank@FY2025}}), while the EBITDA margin sits in the middle of the group.
Capex intensity of {{capex_intensity@FY2025}} is above the peer median of {{capex_intensity.peer_median@FY2025}}, the main offset to the balance-sheet strength.

snapshot.text: Flughafen Wien, the Vienna airport group, grew revenue by {{revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{revenue@FY2025}} in FY2025, but the year carried one-off write-offs from the abandoned third runway project and the deconsolidation of the Get2 security subsidiary.
The EBITDA margin narrowed by {{ebitda_margin.change@FY2025}} to {{ebitda_margin@FY2025}}, and net leverage moved to net cash of {{net_cash@FY2025}} from {{net_cash@FY2024}} in FY2024.

The point to watch is cash generation: free cash flow fell by {{fcf.change@FY2025}} to {{fcf@FY2025}} as capex intensity rose by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2025}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2025}}, above the peer median.

watch_items.text: Cash generation: free cash flow fell by {{fcf.change@FY2025}} to {{fcf@FY2025}} and FFO by {{ffo.change@FY2025}} to {{ffo@FY2025}}, so the investment programme absorbs most of the cash the group generates.

Investment: capex intensity rose by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2025}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2025}}, above the peer median of {{capex_intensity.peer_median@FY2025}}, which keeps pressure on free cash flow.

Liquidity: cash liquidity to revenue fell by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}} as cash and cash-like investments declined by {{cash_like.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_like@FY2025}}.
